request: Design a fixation rod mounted from the top with arm length 200mm to have ability to fix cutting product

actions.operation: Create a fixation rod feature (rod/arm geometry)

parameters.mounting_method: threaded_into_existing_top_boss_bore (assumed, based on existing threaded boss interface)
parameters.rod_major_diameter: match_existing_boss_bore_thread_envelope (derived from FACE 29 radius ~7.0175 => ~14.035 mm nominal; exact thread spec unresolved)
parameters.thread_engagement_length: unresolved (recommend >= 1x to 1.5x nominal diameter, e.g., 14–21 mm if ~M14 class)
parameters.rod_end_feature_for_fixing_product: unresolved (e.g., tapped end hole, clamp block, eyelet, or slotted head)

actions.relational_constraint: Mounted from the top: rod originates from the top threaded boss interface, is coaxial with the boss bore, and seats on/locates from the boss top face; optional secondary anti-rotation/locking interaction can be made with the existing cross-hole if it intersects the bore.
actions.unresolved_reference: Exact rod cross-section/diameter, thread specification (M-size/pitch/class), whether rod is a separate component vs. fused to bracket, whether the rod should be straight (vertical) or an offset/horizontal arm of 200 mm, and the exact end-effector geometry to 'fix cutting product' are not provided.
steps: Localization / intent check (multi-view): identify the mounting 'top' as the Top threaded boss interface (Section S7). Use the boss top face (face_code 0031 / Brep FACE 6) as the primary seating/reference plane, and use the boss bore cylindrical face (face_code 0038 / Brep FACE 29) to define the rod axis and thread matching. Use the boss outer cylindrical wall (face_code 0033 / Brep FACE 5) as a secondary concentric reference if needed.

Create construction geometry: extract/create a datum axis from the cylindrical face of the boss bore (face_code 0038). This axis is the rod centerline. Create/use a sketch plane normal to this axis passing through the boss top face (face_code 0031).

Create rod body (straight rod option, most consistent with 'mounted from the top'): on the plane at boss top (face_code 0031), sketch a circle for the rod shank. Dimension the diameter parametrically to match the intended rod (default: set rod_major_diameter to match the existing bore/thread envelope derived from face_code 0038; keep clearance/fit rules per intended thread/fit).

Extrude/Add solid: extrude the circular sketch along the datum axis away from the bracket (positive +Y direction from the boss top), with extrusion length = arm_length (200 mm). Set operation to New Body (recommended if rod is an assembled part) or Join (if it must be a single-piece bracket+rod).

Add mounting interface on rod (threaded stud): create a second sketch on the rod’s lower end (at/just below boss top face 0031), define a reduced/appropriate thread cylinder length = thread_engagement_length, and create a Revolve/Extrude (if stepped stud is needed). Apply a cosmetic/helix thread feature to match the existing threaded bore (face_code 0038). Add a lead-in chamfer on the stud end (e.g., 1x45°) to aid assembly into the boss; keep the boss top chamfer (face_code 0032) as mating lead-in reference.

Optional locking using existing cross-hole (Section S6): verify if the transverse cross-hole (face_codes 0049/0050; Brep FACE 2/3) intersects the boss bore line. If it does and a locking pin/set-screw is intended, add a matching feature on the rod at the intersection height: (a) for a pin: create a transverse through-hole in the rod aligned to the x-axis so it lines up with the bracket cross-hole; (b) for a set-screw: add a small flat or annular groove on the rod at that height to accept set-screw tip engagement. Keep this step suppressed if intersection/locking is not required.

End feature for 'fix cutting product' (geometry unresolved): at the free end of the 200 mm rod, add a standardized interface as a placeholder—e.g., create a coaxial tapped hole, cross-hole, or a clamp-pad block. Model by sketching on the rod end face and extruding/cutting; add fillets/chamfers for safety. Leave dimensions as parameters awaiting requirements for the cutting product geometry and fixation method.

Edge finishing: apply fillets at rod-to-stud shoulder transitions and chamfers at exposed rod edges to reduce stress concentration and improve handling. Ensure no interference with the existing boss chamfer (face_code 0032) and blend region (face_codes 0034–0037).

intention: Add a fixation rod so the design has the ability to fix/hold a cutting product.

Use the existing top threaded boss interface (S7) as the primary mounting datum to ensure robust load transfer into the upper block (S3) and main upright (S2), minimizing unintended weakening of the base mounting plate (S1).
Optionally leverage the existing transverse cross-hole (S6) as a secondary locking/anti-rotation feature if it intersects the boss/bore region and matches the intended fixation behavior.
